# Draft:Warren Dewey

----
Warren Dewey was an American audio engineer, record producer, and entrepreneur. Known for his contributions in the studio and on location, Dewey’s credits include engineering and mixing for rock bands, as well as work on film and music projects.
Dewey was an influential recording engineer who contributed to numerous charting albums by artists including Boston, Little Feat, Gladys Knight and the Pips, Kiss, Earth Wind and Fire, Sammy Hagar, and The Blues Brothers. Dewey co-recorded the band Boston's self-titled breakout album. Along with producer John Boylan, he is credited with suggesting the band name for Boston.
Dewey was employed by Bell Sound Studios, Mercury Sound, and Jimi Hendrix’s [https://www.nytimes.com/2010/08/26/arts/music/26hendrix.html Electric Lady Studios].
In 2004, Dewey purchased and began restoration on the historic Golden State Theater in Monterey, CA. Dewey had a long love for movie theaters, which began in adolescence while working as a projectionist in upstate New York. During his ownership, Dewey restored the theater to its original 1926 state and brought acts such as, Etta James, Willie Nelson, Firesign Theatre, and more, as well as numerous historic film showings to the theater. He sold the Golden State Theater in 2009 to the Monterey Church.
When the band Kiss recorded their debut album at Bell Sound Studios in New York City, the recording process took six days and the subsequent mixing was carried out by Dewey as the engineer and mixer on that session.
